title: Calibration-driven kernel broker for per-layer mixed-precision dispatch
creator: Asha Patel
description:
We need a runtime 'kernel broker' that chooses per-layer execution precision (FP16 / FP8 / INT8) for each request batch using recently ingested calibration signals and a lightweight cost-accuracy model. Current runtime-level precision switching is coarse-grained and either leaves money on the table or risks avoidable quality regressions. This ticket scopes a safe, observable, and low-overhead decision layer that: 1) consumes per-model and per-layer quantization profiles generated by the offline calibration pipeline, 2) receives periodic online calibration signals (small representative micro-batches or sampled KV-cache deltas) to detect distribution drift, 3) computes a latency/cost/accuracy tradeoff score and picks kernels at layer granularity, 4) logs decisions and confidence for tracing and rollback. The broker must be fast (<100us added per request on p99), support batched requests, integrate with the kernel registry (kernel selection APIs), and provide an emergency fallback to FP16 or a pinned safe route when uncertainty is high. This is intended to be runtime-agnostic (works on Hosted and Dedicated) and compatible with the Private control plane.

Out-of-scope: model re-training, full-blown autoquantization in the runtime, and long-running calibration scheduling (those belong to the calibration pipeline tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Broker elects per-layer kernels using calibration profiles and runtime signals and persists per-request decisions to tracing
End-to-end latency overhead of the broker is <= 100 microseconds median and <= 400 microseconds p99 for 1-8 batch sizes on target hardware (A100 equivalent)
On the standard regression prompt-set (calibration validation set), chosen mixed-precision paths show <= 0.5% relative quality drop vs baseline FP16 when weighted by customer-critical prompts
Token-level cost reduction of >= 10% vs always-FP16 for two representative customer workloads (summarization and chat history-heavy queries) in the staging perf harness
Safe fallback: when online confidence < threshold, runtime routes the request to pinned FP16 path and emits alert telemetry
Unit, integration, and end-to-end tests cover kernel selection logic, batching interactions, and fallback behavior
Documentation and console UI surface: per-model page shows broker-enabled flag, last calibration timestamp, and sampled decision breakdown
technical_notes: Input signals: static quant profiles (per-layer scale/range, profile flavor: symmetric/asymmetric), recent online calibration deltas (sampled activations), and workload metadata (batch size, prompt tokens)

Decision objective: minimize expected cost subject to soft accuracy constraint derived from calibration-driven loss estimate; we implement a linear scoring function: score = alpha * cost_saving - beta * expected_accuracy_drop, where alpha/beta are tunable per-customer defaults

Per-layer action space: {FP16, FP8_e4m3, FP8_e5m2, INT8_affine, INT8_perchannel} mapped to kernel handles. Kernel registry will expose latency and token-cost estimates for each kernel/model shard combination

Calibration cadence: offline calibration runs produce profiles; runtime broker accepts 'freshness' window (default 24h) and can request on-demand micro-calibration (sample up to 32 micro-batches) if drift >= threshold

Safety guards: confidence score threshold, max-consecutive-mixed-precision-fallbacks per request, and a conservative mode that only allows INT8 on layers that passed offline layerwise sensitivity tests

Integration points: kernel-registry API (select_kernel(model, layer, action, batch_shape)), telemetry pipe (span attributes: selected_action, confidence, estimated_delta_accuracy, estimated_cost_saving), and metrics (histograms for decision latency and counters for fallback events)

Batching considerations: broker must consider inter-request heterogeneity; when batch contains mixed-safe-actions, pick the action that satisfies latency SLOs and preserve per-request routing by enqueueing on appropriate kernel shards when supported
Feature flags: runtime flag 'per_layer_broker_v1' with canary rollout via Console rollout policies; default off for existing Dedicated customers until explicit enablement
Evaluation harness: reuse 'calibration-validation' dataset with stratified prompt buckets (short, medium, long) and run A/B experiments across N requests to measure quality and unit-cost changes
tasks: Design: finalize broker API, scoring function parameters, and fail-open rules (owner: Zoe)
Prototype: implement lightweight decision module in runtime as a separate component behind feature flag (owner: Miguel)
Offline: add serializer for per-layer quant profiles into model metadata (owner: Model Onboarding)
Calibration: wire runtime to accept micro-calibration probes and record deltas (owner: Calibration team)
Integration: connect broker to kernel registry and telemetry (owner: Runtime Infra)
Testing: create unit tests for scoring math, integration tests with kernel mocks, and e2e perf runs in staging (owner: SRE/Perf)
Docs: internal design doc and public console help copy (owner: DevEx)
Rollout: staged canary to 5% Hosted, monitor decision latency and accuracy, then increase to Dedicated opt-in customers
comments: 2026-03-01 - Asha Patel: Created ticket after spike showing per-layer variance in quant sensitivity. Initial notes attached to design doc link.
2026-03-04 - Zoe Kim: Proposed scoring prototype and safety thresholds in design doc. Requesting ETA from kernel-registry owners for latency-cost table.

2026-03-06 - Miguel Alvarez: Prototype implemented a naive greedy per-layer selection using precomputed sensitivity scores. Microbenchmarks: median added latency 45us, p99 180us on A100 sim. Cost reduction ~12% on summary workload with small accuracy delta (0.28% on reg set). Pushed draft PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/842

2026-03-08 - Calibration team (note): Offline layerwise sensitivity tests completed for 5 popular models; we observed INT8 safe on 18-32% of layers depending on model size. Sharing profiles in the calibration storage bucket.

2026-03-10 - SRE: Perf harness run shows for batch sizes 1-4 the broker overhead meets median target but p99 needs optimizations under high concurrency. Suggested improvements: cache last-decision per-model-shard and inline fast-path when all layers map to same action.
2026-03-12 - Zoe Kim: Implemented decision cache and added conservative fallback when micro-calibration incomplete. New perf run scheduled; will update metrics by 2026-03-13.

2026-03-13 - Miguel Alvarez: Updated PR with caching and batching-aware tie-breaker. Staging canary ready for 5% traffic. Noted remaining risk: INT8 perchannel kernels sometimes increase memory pressure on small shards; added monitoring alert.
